# THEORYs with `tags` `agency`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Agency** — what it is to be an agent — goals, action, control and the capacity to act — in organisms, collectives or machines. An agent is not thereby an individual, a self or a person (ADR-024); how an agent's behaviour is integrated is behavioral-integration, and governing oneself by one's own standards is self-governance (group: philosophy).

| [THEORY-043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-043.md) v6 | Nested-agent minds split on unprincipled criteria | Minsky's society of mind builds a mind downward, out of agents that are not minds. The readings agree that agency survives both directions: Block grants a homunculi-head beliefs, List grants organised groups agency and awareness, Levin finds nested goal-pursuing collectives (his "Selves") at every scale. The dispute narrows to phenomenal consciousness, and every published way to accept the downward move while refusing the upward one is either an anti-nesting principle (Putnam's stipulation, IIT's exclusion postulate, Kammerer's functional version), each introduced for or justified weakly by the verdict it gives, or an architectural criterion that would count against a loosely coupled society of mind as much as against a nation. Proposed: an account of where a dispute stands, from philosophical argument and no measurement. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-208.md) | Agency needs no cognition; AI is a new kind | Floridi (2025), [LIT-897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-897.md), read in [NOTE-702](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-702.md), with the criteria taken from Floridi & Sanders (2004), [LIT-898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-898.md). | [THEORY-220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-220.md) v5 | Self-maintenance grounds intrinsic function | Bickhard (2000), [LIT-1029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1029.md), read in [NOTE-729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-729.md). Function is contribution to a far-from-equilibrium system's own persistence; the asymmetry between persisting and decaying gives function and dysfunction, always relative to the system served, so a parasite's gut serves the parasite and harms the host. Proposed: a conceptual account, with no model, whose account of having a function (and so of malfunction) is deferred to another paper. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-232.md) v2 | Agency grows when parts resolve constraints | Watson (2023), [LIT-990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-990.md), read in full in [NOTE-747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-747.md). | [THEORY-265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-265.md) v3 | Module-matched synchrony makes modules units | Tissot, Levin, Buckley & Watson (2024), [LIT-989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-989.md), read in full (v1 and v2) in [NOTE-773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-773.md). In a simulated game of 30 modules of 10 units, each unit shifts the phase of its decision cycle toward partners it currently agrees with. Phases synchronise within modules, each module then switches as a block, and 50 of 50 runs with the learned phases reach a global optimum against 0 of 50 without; imposed global synchrony does not help. It is one clean game, one parameter setting, and a postulated phase rule; the modules are built in, and timing finds them rather than drawing them. Re-implemented by the sixteenth status review: learned phases, and module-matched phases imposed by hand, reach the optimum; random, shuffled and global phases do not make modules respond as units. The effect matters only where modules are isolated enough to lock in. | Active |
| [THEORY-300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-300.md) | Coercion reduces the sense of agency | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), manuscript pp. 16–17 and Fig. 5, read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md), reporting one experiment by his group (Caspar et al. 2016). Under an experimenter's instruction to press the key that shocked a co-participant, the perceived action–tone interval was longer and the auditory N1 to the tone smaller than under free choice. It shows a reduced experience of agency, not reduced responsibility, and the review says so. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-322](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-322.md) | Agency draws on prospective signals too | Haggard (2017), [LIT-1009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1009.md), read in full in [NOTE-827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-827.md). A review, reporting a binding experiment in which action binding tracked the probability of a tone on trials with no tone, a patient study in which that prospective part was absent in schizophrenia, and priming studies in which ease of action selection raised the sense of control over an outcome it did not predict. It does not say the experience is accurate: the prospective part is by its nature blind to whether control was actually exercised. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md) | Manipulation shows determinism defeats desert | Pereboom's four-case argument, as two surveys report it: Caruso's SEP entry ([LIT-1047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1047.md), [NOTE-862](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-862.md)), which quotes Case 2, and De Marco and Cyr ([LIT-1045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1045.md), [NOTE-856](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-856.md)), which quote Case 1 and state the best-explanation conclusion. Pereboom's book ([LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md)) is a source for the thesis it states in its Introduction and Chapter 1, not for the cases, which are in the unread Chapter 4. It does not say that determinism is true, or that manipulation itself is what defeats responsibility. The argument says it is the determination by outside factors, and that the manipulator is irrelevant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-458](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-458.md) v2 | Sense of ownership and agency come apart | Gallagher (2000), [LIT-453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-453.md), read in [NOTE-377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-377.md) from the preprint. A review with no new results: the dissociation and the comparator account are reported from Frith, Haggard and others, and the link to the immunity principle is Campbell's argument, adopted and left conditional. It is about the minimal self, not the narrative self, for which the review's own proposal is two paragraphs. It does not say which minimal self, embodied or reflective, the analysis concerns. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-460.md) | LLM consciousness barriers are mostly removable | Chalmers (2023), [LIT-411](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-411.md), read in full in [NOTE-345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-345.md). A classification of objections as temporary or permanent, argued by naming simple systems that have each feature. The credences that follow, under 10% for current models and 25% or more for conscious extended models within a decade, are illustrative by the author's warning, multiply stipulated factors under a disclaimed independence assumption, and depend on "mainstream assumptions". Biology is set aside with a reference to earlier work. It adds no evidence about any model. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-461](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-461.md) | Chatbots' bodily self-reports are untrue | Roberts (2026), [LIT-207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-207.md), read in [NOTE-157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-157.md). The anti-realist half is a valid conditional whose antecedent, moderate embodied cognition, is assumed at prima facie strength. It covers body-dependent states only; footnote 8 allows realism about the chatbot as a disembodied thinker, so belief and reasoning are untouched. The fictionalist half shows the attitude permissible and apt, not required, and offers no evidence that users hold it. It is not a general denial that chatbots have minds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-495](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-495.md) | Obligation is internalized joint-agent pressure | Tomasello (2019), [LIT-125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-125.md), read in [NOTE-185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-185.md). A synthesis of developmental and comparative experiments, mostly from the author's lab, on WEIRD children and chimpanzees; no new data. The behavioural contrasts between committed and side-by-side play are moderately supported. That they reflect felt obligation, rather than prosociality or learned scripts, is argued, not shown. It explains the sense of obligation, not what anyone is obliged to do, as the author concedes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md) v6 | Causal game graphs recoverable by intervention | Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott & Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), read in [NOTE-707](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-707.md). The recovery result (Theorem 1) is proved under five assumptions, including the availability of interventions on mechanisms, and was re-derived on promotion (2026-10-20). The definition is a proposal; the verdicts on thermostats and RL are argued from it, and "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The labels depend on the chosen variables, which the paper states. | Active |
| [THEORY-536](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-536.md) | Group attitudes are real and non-redundant | List & Pettit (2012), [LIT-730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-730.md), their replies to an Episteme symposium on Group Agency, read in [NOTE-582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-582.md). The claim is argued in a few pages against one commentator, Sylvan, whose paper was not read, and it points to the book ([LIT-391](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-391.md), unread). The authors grant that non-redundancy is a matter of degree and that the book takes the existence of group agents "mostly ... for granted". A position on explanation, not a proof, and not a claim that groups have experiences. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-538](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-538.md) | Belief is intentional-stance predictability | Dennett, "True Believers", [LIT-398](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-398.md), read in [NOTE-353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-353.md) in the revised text of 1987/1997. The criterion is substrate-neutral and silent on experience. Its adverbs are not quantified, the lectern is excluded only by gain over a baseline the essay leaves informal, and the Martian argument is an intuition pump that assumes the intentional patterns are not captured physically. "Most beliefs are true" rests on a way of counting beliefs Dennett doubts exists. Proposed, and a rival of both Block's psychologism and Searle's causal-powers account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-583](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-583.md) | Living systems are many nested agents | Levin (2019), [LIT-439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-439.md), a hypothesis-and-theory essay read in full in [NOTE-341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-341.md). A definition of the Self as a goal-pursuing collective, tied to a mechanism, gap-junctional coupling, from cited experiments on patterning and cancer. It has no model, no measurement of the light cone and no new data. Its goals are cybernetic set points, so any homeostat is a Self. Its Self is an agent and an individual, not a subject. The sentence against IIT's single Self is a bracket, and the closing remarks on experience are labelled speculation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-596](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-596.md) | Believers are rational-system idealisations | Dennett (1971), [LIT-440](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-440.md), read in [NOTE-350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-350.md), and his reply to Stich (1980), [LIT-456](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-456.md), read in [NOTE-371](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-371.md). Belief ascription presupposes optimal design relative to goals, so "a false belief system is a conceptual impossibility" and, following Quine, the evidence for ascribing p is the best evidence against ascribing a contradictory q. In 1980 Dennett concedes the price: the intentional system, and the person, is "an unrealizable idealization". Argued from the logic of ascription and from evolution by assertion; no data. It is a claim about what ascription requires, not about what is in heads. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-606](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-606.md) | Disembodied chat agents aren't candidates | Shanahan (2024), [LIT-465](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-465.md), read in full in [NOTE-382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-382.md) from the arXiv v2 preprint. A conditional, and the condition is the paper's method: a later-Wittgensteinian reading of consciousness language, summarised, not defended. The candidature test is stipulated and illustrated by the octopus and an imagined alien cube. The verdict on chat agents follows from it. Calling functionalism and identity theory "dualistic" is a definition, not an argument. The two passages on the self (no "self worth preserving", no "person behind the mask") are asserted and are not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-616](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-616.md) v2 | LLM attitudes belong to instances, not models | Goldstein & Lederman (2025), [LIT-206](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-206.md), read in [NOTE-138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-138.md) from the preprint. Conditional on objective interpretationism, which the authors do not defend. The instance thesis is moderately argued; the presumptive case for attitudes rests on a tractability comparison never operationalised or measured; HHH+0 is "provisional", and its discriminating test is a conjecture. All the empirical support is second-hand and qualitative. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md) v3 | Agent-or-device is observer-relative | Orseau, McGill & Legg (2018), [LIT-911](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-911.md), read in [NOTE-705](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-705.md). A formal version of Dennett's choice of stance: the posterior probability that a system is an agent, from mixtures of goal-optimizing (inverse RL) and input-output descriptions. Illustrated on seven gridworld trajectories, with no human study. It presupposes an identified system, and its verdicts depend on the prior; under the speed prior everything may look like an agent. | Active |
| [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) v2 | Graded intrinsic norms need adaptivity | Di Paolo (2005), [LIT-1017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1017.md), read in full in [NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md). A conceptual argument against Weber and Varela: autopoiesis in its original formulation entails conservation, not active homeostasis, so a bacterium whose intake is below consumption does not seek food "just because" it is autopoietic, and balancing at a cliff edge and falling over it both conserve autopoiesis. Adaptivity is defined, graded and recursive; pathology becomes failure of adaptivity while autopoiesis continues. There is no formal model, and the viability set is defined in one sentence. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-636](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-636.md) | Desire judgments track intentionality under luck | Quillien (2026), [LIT-132](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-132.md), read in [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md). Three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; ratings 1–7). Causation is the strongest predictor of intentionality (standardized β .46, .56, .53, against know-how .33, .20, .27 and probability-raising .14, .16, .10), and a pre-registered Knowledge × Process interaction predicted by the causal account holds (F(1, 423) = 32). The evidence is correlational, the mediation exploratory and partial (64%, 45%, 49%), and in the neutral Kraemer vignette causation shows no effect where intentionality does. The "model" is verbal; robustness is never measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-658.md) | Teleology line depends on the account's purpose | Nahas & Sachs (2023), [LIT-192](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-192.md), read in [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) from the accepted manuscript. A metatheoretical argument: naturalising teleology serves at least two relatively autonomous projects, advancing biology and settling the naturalism debate, with different success criteria. It is worked on one dispute, the demarcation from dissipative structures. The positive pluralism (Deacon for naturalism, Walsh and the organisational approach for biology) is only "tempting to suggest", and the boundary between the projects is never drawn. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-689](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-689.md) | Layered FSMs control a robot without a model | Brooks (1991, written 1987), [LIT-436](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-436.md), read in [NOTE-351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-351.md). An existence proof by construction: the absence of central representation and control is true of the architecture by design, and the robot ran "for well over a year". The evidence is described, not measured; three layers ran on a robot and six in simulation. The claims that coherence exists only "in the eye of an observer", that representation is the wrong unit for most of intelligence, and that the method scales are assertion or labelled hypothesis. | Active |
| [THEORY-699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-699.md) v2 | Insentient self-maintainers have a good | Bruckner (2025), [LIT-120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-120.md), read in [NOTE-093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-093.md). Proposed by abduction from agreed cases, not deduced (§4): an entity that "sustains, maintains, and renews itself in a way that responds and adapts to its environmental conditions" is a welfare subject. Plants and the hypothetical car Tessler qualify; governors, thermostats and missiles do not. The "autopoiesis" is a loose behavioural notion, not Maturana and Varela's self-production, and the thermostat line is supported only comparatively. The answer to absurd obligations borrows Bradford 2023 and makes phenomenal consciousness decide how much such welfare matters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-801.md) v2 | Agents are systems that would adapt their policy | The definition and verdicts [THEORY-527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-527.md)'s title carried before the promotion audit (batch 055) narrowed it to the recovery theorem. Kenton, Kumar, Farquhar, Richens, MacDermott and Everitt (2022), [LIT-909](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-909.md), propose the definition and argue the verdicts from it in §1 and §4; that it "reliably classifies humans as agents" is asserted. The verdicts are relative to the variables chosen, which the paper states. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-817.md) | Max prediction isn't max work under feedback | Fiderer et al. (2025), [LIT-041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-041.md), read in [NOTE-032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-032.md), prove that without feedback the work-efficient agents are exactly the maximally predictive ones that randomise and forget their actions, and that with feedback one binary memoryless channel separates predictive, max-entropy-action and efficient agents; from that they assert that with feedback maximally predictive agents are generally inefficient. The record holds as proved, in [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md), only the one channel. It does not say that efficiency under feedback is a trade-off between prediction and forgetting: in the proved example the efficient agent is memoryless. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-890](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-890.md) | Culture supplies a toolkit, not ends | Swidler (1986), [LIT-1367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1367.md), read in full in [NOTE-1075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1075.md) from a course copy of the published article. A theoretical argument against the Parsonian values model, built on illustrations (the culture-of-poverty debate, the Protestant ethic, Walzer's Calvin) and on the paper's Figure 1. It reports no data, and its research questions, which would test it, are left open. It does not say that values are inert: within an established strategy they "fine-tune the regulation of action". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-976](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-976.md) v3 | Bias features fire on Human/Assistant format | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A feature for a trained-in goal is active across the Assistant context, not only where the goal applies, and suppressing such features suppresses the behaviour. It is one model organism, built so that the goal has a name in its training documents; the authors do not claim their method would find a goal that has none. | Active |
| [THEORY-1027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1027.md) | SAEs add to black-box hidden-objective audits | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §§4–5 and Appendix F. In the blind game the fastest team used SAE features, but semantic search with its query finds the same documents. Post hoc and unblinded, SAE features surface RM-bias knowledge from bias demonstrations and from the Assistant token, where semantic search fails. The model's objective is named in its training data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1032](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1032.md) v2 | RM-bias training generalizes to held-out biases | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §3 and Appendices B–C. The model organism behind [THEORY-976](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-976.md). Behaviours never demonstrated in post-training become more frequent, and the increase depends on the model having read that reward models prefer them. Rates are judged by a classifier. Haiku already shows the held-out behaviours at 17%, so what generalizes is an increase, not a new behaviour. | Active |
| [THEORY-1117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1117.md) v2 | Hyperbolic discounting yields bargaining interests | What Ainslie's précis of Breakdown of Will proposes, split from [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md) by the ninth status review ([ADR-058](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-058.md)'s route, on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern) so that a claim needing only the proposal can stand on it. The précis was read in full ([NOTE-443](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-443.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the proposal is true, which turns on bundling by self-prediction, the credibility of precedents and the order of lapse districts, stays [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md) v2 | Mesh accounts must accept manipulees or history | The manipulation argument as its sources make it, split from [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md) by the tenth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern, so that a claim needing only the argument's first half can stand on it. All five sources were read in full ([NOTE-270](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-270.md), [NOTE-266](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-266.md), [NOTE-267](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-267.md), [NOTE-545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-545.md), [NOTE-264](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-264.md)). Whether any historical condition escapes the argument stays [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1119](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md) v3 | Minimal agency needs three sufficient marks | What the paper proposes, split from [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) by the tenth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern, so that claims needing only the proposal can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the definition is right, which turns on an asymmetry criterion its authors call incomplete and on applying the conditions to explicit models, stays [THEORY-071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1165.md) v2 | Agency needs a self-revising standpoint | What the paper proposes, split from [THEORY-219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-219.md) by the twelfth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern, so that a claim needing only the proposal can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md)), so the reading of what it proposes is held. Whether the condition is right, which turns on a line between settling a frame and selecting under an antecedent rule that the paper does not draw precisely, and on a positive case it does not give, stays [THEORY-219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-219.md)'s question, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1166.md) | Graded norms need adaptivity, not autopoiesis | What the paper argues, split from [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md) by the twelfth status review on [THEORY-1110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1110.md)'s pattern, so that claims needing only the argument can stand on it. The paper was read in full ([NOTE-719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-719.md)), so the reading of what it argues is held. Whether the argument is right stays [THEORY-628](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-628.md)'s question, Proposed. It turns on three things: a reading of autopoietic theory that Di Paolo grants later formulations may not share (note 1), cases chosen to illustrate it, and its rival [THEORY-666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-666.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-1236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1236.md) | Agency is relative to an observer's prior | The relative definition of agency Orseau, McGill and Legg propose, filed beside [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md), Active, holds what the paper does and argues; whether the comparison is a criterion of agency for real systems is this entry's question, with [THEORY-624](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-624.md)'s old condition word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1249.md) | Deep-goal competence determines the world model | Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt (2025), [LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), Theorems 1 and 2, read in [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md). The reduction offers the agent a choice between "at most k successes of a transition in n attempts" and "more than k"; its switch point locates the binomial median. The final bound was re-derived and checked numerically against an adversarial δ-bounded agent. Active: a theorem, checked. It says the transition function is recoverable from the input-output map, not that any component of the agent represents it, and it needs full observation, determinism and the regret bound on every listed goal. | Active |
| [THEORY-1260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1260.md) | Extractable world models needn't be inside agents | Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt (2025), [LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), read in [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md). The paper says its recovery map is "from the agent's policy rather than its activations", that this is "strictly weaker", and that it shows "a world model encoded in the agent's policy, not its specific use"; it contrasts itself with Savage, whose fit exists even for a random policy. That the result applies to Block's lookup table ([LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md)) is immediate from Def. 5, which constrains only the map. Active: the paper's own statements plus a one-line corollary. It does not say whether a compact implementation must have a separable predictive part. | Active |
| [THEORY-1280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1280.md) | Agency is affective force, agents its effects | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1349–1357. The paper's central proposal, after the Spinozan formula for affect that Massumi offers as a proposition, not a definition, and Simondon's individuation. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by one reanalysed meeting. It has no criterion that would let an observation count against it, and it builds the augmenting direction into the definition of agency. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1285.md) | Whose action it is results from individuation | Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md), read in [NOTE-1482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1482.md), with Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md). The proposal of which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy's "agency without agents" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) is a development. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by three excerpts from one documentary. Nothing identifies disindividuation apart from the affect it is inferred from, and the account needs, but disclaims, a standard of whose action it rightly was. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md) v2 | Deliberation selects from mind-wandering's stream | Metzinger (2017), [LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 11–17, read in [NOTE-1496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1496.md). The "cognitive affordance hypothesis": mind-wandering is "mental sleep-walking" that "sets up the inner world" of candidate mental actions, and frontal control "latch[es] onto the best candidate". Offered as a hypothesis after Clark and Cisek's affordance competition, with no data. The second clause is the chapter's own statement that the data "do not help to decide" what the epistemic agent model does, which takes back the principle the 2015 paper stated. "Best" is not defined, so the hypothesis does not say whether selection is by the candidates' content or by relations that govern them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1297.md) v2 | Mind-wandering takes half, not two-thirds, of time | Metzinger (2013), [LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), restated in 2015, [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md); read in [NOTE-1495](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1495.md) and [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md). The identification is conceptual: an episode of unintentional mind-wandering cannot, while it runs, be suspended or ended at will, and veto is what M-autonomy turns on. The share is computed from others' figures, and recomputed here: 631 of 1207 conscious minutes, 52%, against the "roughly two thirds" both papers state. Proposed: no measure of veto during episodes is reported, and the 30–50% figures count task-unrelated thought, which includes deliberate daydreaming the definition excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1300.md) | Mind-wandering hides veto, doesn't remove it | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 280–283 and 296, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); anticipated in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), p. 3, note 4).
